test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Electronic Mechanic) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Why is a braking system used in an energy meter?

options.text: To reduce the power consumption of the meter itself
To increase the speed of the rotating disk
To maintain a uniform rotation proportional to power consumption
To decrease the friction in the moving parts

solution:
In an **energy meter (induction type)**, the aluminium disc rotates due to the interaction of magnetic fields produced by the current and voltage coils.
If there were **no braking system**, the disc would rotate too fast and give **incorrect energy readings**.

The **braking system** (usually a permanent magnet) produces a **braking torque** that is proportional to the speed of the disc. This ensures that:

 
• 
 
The disc speed remains **steady**

 
 
• 
 
The speed of rotation is **directly proportional to the power consumption**

 
 
• 
 
Accurate measurement of electrical energy is obtained
